On February 23, 2016, Astro released their debut extended play *[Spring Up](/wiki/Spring_Up "Spring Up")* alongside its [lead single](/wiki/Lead_single "Lead single") "Hide & Seek".[[15]](#cite_note-15) For two days, starting on February 22, 2016, showcases and press conferences were held at Lotte Card Art Center[[16]](#cite_note-16) and Wapop Concert Hall[[17]](#cite_note-17) to commemorate the group's first release. Within a week of its release, *Spring Up* reached number six on the [*Billboard* World Albums Chart](/wiki/Billboard_chart "Billboard chart") in the United States,[[18]](#cite_note-18) as well as number four on the [Gaon Album Chart](/wiki/Circle_Album_Chart "Circle Album Chart").
[[19]](#cite_note-19) On February 25, the group released the [music video](/wiki/Music_video "Music video") for "Cat's Eye" (장화 신은 고양이), containing clips from their web drama *To Be Continued*. On April 13, Astro was the only Korean act invited to the LeTV Entertainment Awards in China.[[20]](#cite_note-20)

Their second extended play *[Summer Vibes](/wiki/Summer_Vibes "Summer Vibes")* was released on July 1.[[21]](#cite_note-21) The album peaked at number six on the *Billboard* World Albums Chart[[22]](#cite_note-22) and at number two on the Gaon Album Chart.[[23]](#cite_note-23) Furthermore, the music video for "Breathless" (숨가빠), featuring labelmate [Choi Yoo-jung](/wiki/Choi_Yoo-jung_(singer) "Choi Yoo-jung (singer)") of [Weki Meki](/wiki/Weki_Meki "Weki Meki"), surpassed half a million views in just three days.[[24]](#cite_note-24) The same month, on July 31, Astro performed in front of more than 20,000 people at [Staples Center](/wiki/Staples_Center "Staples Center") in Los Angeles for [KCON 2016](/w/index.php?title=KCON_2016&action=edit&redlink=1 "KCON 2016 (page does not exist)").[[25]](#cite_note-25)[[26]](#cite_note-26)

**Mongolia**[[b]](#cite_note-11)[[c]](#cite_note-12) is a [landlocked country](/wiki/Landlocked_country "Landlocked country") in the [East Asia](/wiki/East_Asia "East Asia") region. It is bordered by [Russia](/wiki/Russia "Russia") to the north and [China](/wiki/China "China") to the south, and covers an area of 1,564,116 square kilometers (603,909 square miles), making it the [18th-largest country](/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_area "List of countries and dependencies by area") in the world and the second largest landlocked country after [Kazakhstan](/wiki/Kazakhstan "Kazakhstan"), as well as the largest landlocked country that does not border an [inland sea](/wiki/Endorheic_basin "Endorheic basin"). With a population of 3.5 million, Mongolia is the world's [most sparsely populated sovereign state](/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_population_density "List of countries and dependencies by population density"), excluding partially unrecognized [Western Sahara](/wiki/Sahrawi_Arab_Democratic_Republic "Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic"). The country constitutes a significant portion of the [Mongolian Plateau](/wiki/Mongolian_Plateau "Mongolian Plateau"), and its natural environment is characterized by grassy [steppe](/wiki/Steppe "Steppe"), mountains to the north and west, and the [Gobi Desert](/wiki/Gobi_Desert "Gobi Desert") to the south. [Ulaanbaatar](/wiki/Ulaanbaatar "Ulaanbaatar"), the capital and [largest city](/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Mongolia "List of cities in Mongolia"), is home to roughly half of the country's population.

The territory of modern-day Mongolia has been ruled by various [nomadic empires](/wiki/Nomadic_empire "Nomadic empire"), including the [Xiongnu](/wiki/Xiongnu "Xiongnu"), the [Xianbei](/wiki/Xianbei "Xianbei"), the [Rouran](/wiki/Rouran "Rouran"), the [First Turkic Khaganate](/wiki/First_Turkic_Khaganate "First Turkic Khaganate"), the [Second Turkic Khaganate](/wiki/Second_Turkic_Kh

He trained in martial arts at the Krauseworld Academy in Glasgow under brothers Steve Krause and Mike Krause where he achieved Phase 4 rank in both [Jeet Kune Do](/wiki/Jeet_Kune_Do "Jeet Kune Do") and [Filipino Kali](/wiki/Eskrima "Eskrima").[[14]](#cite_note-14) He topped a list of the 100 Most Eligible Men in Scotland in 2002.

A reception was held afterwards for about 130 guests.

Boyd has a [tattoo](/wiki/Tattoo "Tattoo") of the Elvish word for "nine" written with the [Tengwar](/wiki/Tengwar "Tengwar") script, a reference to his involvement in *The Lord of the Rings*, and the fact that his character was one of the nine members of the *[Fellowship of the Ring](/wiki/Fellowship_of_the_Ring_(characters) "Fellowship of the Ring (characters)")*. Cabernet Franc is lighter than Cabernet Sauvignon,[[1]](#cite_note-Discovery-1) making a bright pale red wine[[2]](#cite_note-winepro-2) that contributes finesse and lends a [peppery](/wiki/Black_pepper "Black pepper")

Under the direction of [Liu Qi](/wiki/Liu_Qi_(politician,_born_1942) "Liu Qi (politician, born 1942)"), Beijing was elected as the host city for the 2008 Summer Olympics on 13 July 2001, during the [112th](/wiki/List_of_IOC_meetings "List of IOC meetings") [IOC](/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") Session in Moscow, defeating bids from Toronto, Paris, [Istanbul](/wiki/Istanbul "Istanbul"), and [Osaka](/wiki/Osaka "Osaka"). Prior to the session, five other cities ([Bangkok](/wiki/Bangkok "Bangkok"), [Cairo](/wiki/Cairo "Cairo"), [Havana](/wiki/Havana "Havana"), [Kuala Lumpur](/wiki/Kuala_Lumpur "Kuala Lumpur"), and [Seville](/wiki/Seville "Seville")) had submitted bids to the IOC, but failed to make the short list chosen by the IOC Executive Committee in 2000. After the first round of voting, Beijing held a significant lead over the other four candidates. Osaka received only six votes and was eliminated. In the second round, Beijing was supported by a [majority](/wiki/Majority "Majority") of voters, eliminating the need for subsequent rounds.[[11]](#cite_note-Election-15) Toronto's bid was its fifth loss since 1960 (failed bids for 1960, 1964, 1976 and 1996 Games, losing to Rome, Tokyo, Montreal and Atlanta).[[12]](#cite_note-16)

When bidding for the Games, Beijing actually proposed different dates (25 July – 10 August for the Olympics and 27 August – 7 September for the Paralympics).[[13]](#cite_note-17)

Members of the IOC did not disclose their votes, but news reports speculated that broad international support led to China's selection, especially from developing nations that had received assistance from China to construct stadiums. Results were expected by the end of 2011; however, 13% of families did not return their forms. The official language of San Marino is [Italian](/wiki/Italian_language "Italian language").[[133]](#cite_note-137) The Sammarinese dialect of [Romagnol](/wiki/Romagnol_language "Romagnol language") is also spoken, mainly by the elderly. It is considered an [endangered language](/wiki/Endangered_language "Endangered language").[[134]](#cite_note-138)

Languages of the United States :: part 05 :: chunk_0004
The most commonly used language in the [United States](/wiki/United_States "United States") is English (specifically [American English](/wiki/American_English "American English")), which is the [national language](/wiki/National_language "National language") and *[de facto](/wiki/De_facto "De facto")* [official language](/wiki/Official_language "Official language"). While the U.S. has no statutory official language, the federal government primarily uses English and a 2025 [executive order](/wiki/Executive_Order_14224 "Executive Order 14224") declared English official.[[1]](#cite_note-EOWP-2)[[2]](#cite_note-EONYT-3) In addition, 32 U.S. states out of 50 and all five [U.S. territories](/wiki/U.S._territories "U.S. territories") have laws that recognize English as an official language, with three states and most territories having adopted English plus one or more other official languages. Overall, 430 languages are spoken or [signed](/wiki/Sign_language "Sign language") by the population, of which 177 are [indigenous to the U.S. or its territories](#Indigenous_languages),[[7]](#cite_note-8) and accommodations for non-English-language speakers are sometimes made under various federal, state, and local laws.

The majority of the [U.S. population](/wiki/Demographics_of_the_United_States "Demographics of the United States") (77%) speaks only English at home as of 2024, according to the [American Community Survey](/wiki/American_Community_Survey "American Community Survey") (ACS) of the [U.S. Census Bureau](/wiki/U.S._Census_Bureau "U.S. Census Bureau").[[8]](#cite_note-:3-9) The second most common language by far is [Spanish](/wiki/Spanish_language_in_the_United_States "Spanish language in the United States"), spoken by 13.9% of the population,[[8]](#cite_note-:3-9) followed by [Chinese](/wiki/Chinese_language_in_the_United_States "Chinese language in the United States"), spoken by around 1% of the population. They were awarded a spot in the league to replace the [Worcester baseball team](/wiki/Worcester_Worcesters "Worcester Worcesters"), a franchise that had folded in 1882. The new team was nicknamed the "Phillies" from the start, and immediately compiled a .173 [winning percentage](/wiki/Winning_percentage "Winning percentage"), which stands as the worst in franchise history. Although many sources (including the Phillies themselves) claim that Reach and Rogers bought the Brown Stockings and moved them to Philadelphia, all available evidence suggests this is not the case. Significantly, no players from Worcester[[18]](#cite_note-18) ended up with the 1883 Quakers.[[19]](#cite_note-19)

In [1884](/wiki/1884_Philadelphia_Quakers_season "1884 Philadelphia Quakers season"), [Harry Wright](/wiki/Harry_Wright "Harry Wright"), the former manager of baseball's first openly professional team, the [Cincinnati Red Stockings](/wiki/Cincinnati_Red_Stockings "Cincinnati Red Stockings"), was recruited as a manager in hopes of reversing the team's fortunes.[[20]](#cite_note-TBT-20)

[William Herschel](/wiki/William_Herschel "William Herschel"), discoverer of Uranus

Before its recognition as a planet, Uranus had been observed many times, but was generally misidentified as a star. It was apparently observed by [Hipparchus](/wiki/Hipparchus "Hipparchus"), who measured the positions of stars in 128 BC for his catalog that was later incorporated into [Ptolemy](/wiki/Ptolemy "Ptolemy")'s *[Almagest](/wiki/Almagest "Almagest")*. The catalog gives the positions of four stars forming a quadrilateral in [Virgo](/wiki/Virgo_(constellation) "Virgo (constellation)"). One of the four stars does not exist, but Uranus was at that position in April of 128 BC.[[29]](#cite_note-35) The earliest definite sighting was in 1690, when [John Flamsteed](/wiki/John_Flamsteed "John Flamsteed") observed it at least six times, cataloguing it as 34 [Tauri](/wiki/Taurus_(constellation) "Taurus (constellation)"). [James Bradley](/wiki/James_Bradley "James Bradley") observed it three times, in 1748, 1750, and 1753. [Tobias Mayer](/wiki/Tobias_Mayer "Tobias Mayer") observed it once in 1756. The French astronomer [Pierre Charles Le Monnier](/wiki/Pierre_Charles_Le_Monnier "Pierre Charles Le Monnier") observed Uranus at least twelve times between 1750 and 1769, including on four consecutive nights.[[30]](#cite_note-36)

[William Herschel](/wiki/William_Herschel "William Herschel") observed Uranus on 13 March 1781 from the garden of his house at 19 New King Street in [Bath, Somerset](/wiki/Bath,_Somerset "Bath, Somerset"), England (now the [Herschel Museum of Astronomy](/wiki/Herschel_Museum_of_Astronomy "Herschel Museum of Astronomy")),[[31]](#cite_note-37) and initially reported it (on 26 April 1781) as a [comet](/wiki/Comet "Comet").[[32]](#cite_note-Ref-1-38) With a homemade 6.

Luxembourg is one of Europe's smallest countries, ranking [168th](/wiki/List_of_countries_by_area "List of countries by area") in size of the [194 independent countries of the world](/wiki/List_of_sovereign_states "List of sovereign states"); it is about 2,586 square kilometres (998 sq mi) in size, measuring 82 km (51 mi) long and 57 km (35 mi) wide. It lies between latitudes [49°](/wiki/49th_parallel_north "49th parallel north") and [51° N](/wiki/51st_parallel_north "51st parallel north"), and longitudes [5°](/wiki/5th_meridian_east "5th meridian east") and [7° E](/wiki/7th_meridian_east "7th meridian east").[[94]](#cite_note-97)

To the east, Luxembourg borders the German *[Bundesländer](/wiki/States_of_Germany "States of Germany")* of [Rhineland-Palatinate](/wiki/Rhineland-Palatinate "Rhineland-Palatinate") and [Saarland](/wiki/Saarland "Saarland"), and to the south, it borders the French *[région](/wiki/Regions_of_France "Regions of France")* of [Grand Est](/wiki/Grand_Est "Grand Est") ([Lorraine](/wiki/Lorraine "Lorraine")). The Grand Duchy borders Belgium's [Wallonia](/wiki/Wallonia "Wallonia"), in particular the Belgian [provinces](/wiki/Provinces_of_Belgium "Provinces of Belgium") of [Luxembourg](/wiki/Luxembourg_(Belgium) "Luxembourg (Belgium)") and [Liège](/wiki/Li%C3%A8ge_Province "Liège Province"), part of which comprises the [German-speaking Community of Belgium](/wiki/German-speaking_Community_of_Belgium "German-speaking Community of Belgium")

Luffy ranked first in all of *[One Piece](/wiki/One_Piece "One Piece") Characters Official Popularity Poll*.[[n 3]](#cite_note-67) The only main protagonists that achieved ranked first in all of their correspondent popularity polls are Luffy and [Gintoki Sakata](/wiki/Gintoki_Sakata "Gintoki Sakata").[[65]](#cite_note-68)[[66]](#cite_note-69)[[67]](#cite_note-70)[[68]](#cite_note-71)[[69]](#cite_note-72) On *The 1st Global One Piece Characters Popularity Poll*, the latest official popularity poll of *One Piece* in which more than 12 million voted from all over the world, Luffy topped the list having total votes of 1,637,921.[[70]](#cite_note-73)

Due to the character's popularity, allusions to Luffy have been made in several Japanese manga and anime, as well as Western comics and television series.[[71]](#cite_note-74)

[NTT](/wiki/Nippon_Telegraph_and_Telephone "Nippon Telegraph and Telephone") customers chose Luffy as their second-favorite black-haired male anime character.[[72]](#cite_note-75) The Gum-Gum Gatling technique topped the male category in a Japanese survey of the most popular moves in manga and anime.[[73]](#cite_note-76) Luffy was even nominated in the Best Male Character category for the 2008 Society for the Promotion of Japanese Animation Awards.[[74]](#cite_note-77)[[75]](#cite_note-78) He ranked 22nd on Chris Mackenzie's IGN list of top-25 anime characters of all time.[[76]](#cite_note-79)

In August 2017, a Japanese TV special voted Luffy the 8th "strongest hero" from the [Showa Era](/wiki/Showa_Era "Showa Era") as well as the 4th one from the [Heisei Era](/wiki/Heisei_Era "Heisei Era").[[77]](#cite_note-80) At the [8th Crunchyroll Anime Awards](/wiki/8th_Crunchyroll_Anime_Awards "8th Crunchyroll Anime Awards") in 2024, Luffy won [Best Main Character](/wiki/Crunchyroll_Anime_Award_for_Best_Character#Best_Main_Character "Crunchyroll Anime Award for Best Character
